'0.4 A scheme for labelling environment friendly pmduetsto be known IS ECO Mark has been introduced at tbe instance of the Ministry of Environment and Forests ( MEF). 1. SCOPE
1.1 This standard prescri~s the requ-irements and the methods of sampling and test for nigerseed oil.

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of l this standard, the definitions given under 2 of 1S : 548�1964 Methods Sampling and Test for Oils and Fats (Revised), a nd also those given below shall apply.

or

2.1.1 Refined Nigerseed Oil -:- Nige~seed oil obtained by the proce~s of expression or solvent extracnon which has been refined by neutralszarion with alkali, bleached with bleaching earth or active carbon or both, and deodorized with Iteam, no other chemical agents being used. Z.1.2 Semi-refined Niger,eed Oi/- Nigerseed oil obtained by the process of solvent-eatraction which hal been neutralized with alkali.

3. TYPES AND GRADES
3.1 The material shall be of the following type. and grades:

a) E%pre",d
b) So/,en' ExtrDcled: Refined Grade, Semi-rdined Grade, and

Grade 1 (Raw).
3.1.1 The semi-refined grade and the grade 1 (raw) of the solventextracted type are suitable for making VAN.A.SP.4TI and refined oil, and are not for direct edible consumption.

4. REQ,UIRBMENTS
t.1 The material shall be obtained from clean and sound seeds of niger plant GUi,eDIUllJbyssyniea Cass., fam. Compositz, by a process of expression or by a process of solvent extraction:It ..han-be clear and free Crom rancidity, adulteraDts~ sediment, suspended and other foreign matter, sep~ rated water and added colouring andtftavouring substances.

4.1.1 The clarity of the material shall be judged by the absence of turbidity after keeping the fil~ sample at sere for 24 houn. 4.1.2 Solvent-exl.racted oil .ball be obtained Crom the oleaginoUi
